text:
sam: FYI ran profiling on the canary for the fused-attn epilogue changes (PR #2789). Mixed results: kernel time down, epilogue and paging overhead up. posting numbers and a short thread. :eyes:

jia: thanks — can you drop the perf summary? interested in p95 tail impact.

sam: sure, quick nvprof summary from a 1k-token streaming workload (seq=1024 distribution w/ many small batches):
```
nvprof (aggregate):
 fused_attn_qkv_pack      32.4 ms   (45.0%)
 flash_attn_forward      20.1 ms   (28.0%)
 epilogue_write_kv        8.9 ms   (12.4%)
 memcpy_h2d               5.1 ms    (7.1%)
 other                    5.5 ms    (7.5%)
 total                    72.0 ms
 tokens/sec (end-to-end)  ~1.1k
 p50 latency              68 ms
 p95 latency             210 ms  (tail is worse than baseline)
```

marco: what's the batch shape distribution? streaming workloads usually give tiny micro-batches which wreck kernel efficiency. also: are we seeing extra memcpy because of paged KV layout?

sam: batch sizes are mostly 1-4 (streaming completions). We switched to a paged KV layout to support large contexts; writes now often touch a whole 64KB page even for a few tokens which causes write amplification and extra copies when we currently materialize the QKV output in a temp buffer before appending to the page.

lina: sounds like an opportunity to fuse the epilogue to write directly into the KV page. if we can emit Q/K/V into the final page address with bias+rope applied inline we avoid the extra memcpy. also combine bias+rope in the same kernel to reduce passes.

jia: agree but watch out for quantization paths. for 8-bit packed models we currently do pack/unpack in separate steps; in-place pack while applying rope/bias may complicate correctness.

sam: noted. quick A/B microbench:
- A: current canary (QKV pack -> temp -> memcpy -> page)
- B: epilogue-fused write (compute -> direct write to KV page, bias+rope fused)
B lowered kernel % for fused_attn_qkv_pack by ~20% and p50 improved ~6%, but p95 regressed in some traces due to page allocator contention and increased single-threaded work in the epilogue.

deploy-bot: canary rollout status: 5% traffic -> anomalies detected in p95 latency, auto-halting further rollout. See /deploys/2789. :warning:

marco: two follow-ups:
 1) add per-stream preallocated page pools to eliminate allocator contention. try lock-free freelist if possible.
 2) experiment with a batching heuristic that coalesces small streaming requests into micro-batches when latency headroom allows (heuristic: wait up to 4ms or until N=8 tokens queued).

lina: +1 on direct-write epilogue, but we should also explore fusing bias+rope at vectorized level (fewer FMAs). Could shave ~1.5-3ms on long seqs.

jia: I'll prototype in-place pack with saturation checks for int8 path to avoid correctness issues. if that works, the memcopy disappears for quantized models too.

sam: here's the bench command I used (bench harness under infra/bench):
```
./bench_attn --model=gpt2 --seq=1024 --workload=streaming --bs-dist="1:0.6,2:0.25,4:0.15" --measure=nvprof --out=artifacts/2789
```
results in artifacts/2789/profile-*.npy and a small csv with kernel breakdown.

marco: can someone add counters for page_write_amp and pages_allocated in the runtime metrics? we need numbers to decide whether prealloc or coalescing is better.

lina: i'll add tracepoints for pages_allocated, pages_reused, bytes_written_to_pages.

sam: thanks — jia, can you run variant B on a 10% canary (offline) with prealloc enabled? marco, can you prototype the micro-batcher? i'll open follow-up PRs for the epilogue change and a rollback patch if the canary stays halted.

jia: will run now. estimate 2 hours. :rocket:

marco: prototyping micro-batcher this afternoon, will post diff.

sam: quick note — avoid changing routing fallback in the same PR; keep the epilogue/pack changes isolated. we want narrow canaries to understand regressed tail. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: roll halted at 5%. Manual approval required to continue.

sam: final — summary and next actions will be in GH issue #2789-comment. will post perf CSV and flamegraphs when available. thanks all.
